newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Malan denies foreign exchange tax report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Malan denies foreign exchange tax report.

text.p: Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan denied that the government was considering a 25 percent tax on foreign exchange transactions, a ministry spokesman said.
"There is absolutely no intention on the part of the government to tax foreign exchange (deals)," the spokesman said.

The newspaper Gazeta Mercantil said in its Monday edition that the Federal Tax Secretariat was mulling a 25 percent Financial Operations Tax which would apply to dividend payments and to operations outside Brazil to raise capital.
The ministry spokesman said neither Malan nor tax boss Everardo Maciel knew of the existence of a supposed tax secretariat study cited by Gazeta.
"There are hundreds of studies being drawn up by second and third-tier economists but that doesn't mean the government intends to put them into effect," the spokesman said.
